title: Alibaba HappyShrimp AI Music App Launches on iOS, Android
summary: Alibaba's HappyShrimp AI music generator launches November 14, 2026 on iOS and Android with text-to-song creation in 7 styles. Pricing starts at $14.90/month.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Alibaba officially released HappyShrimp on iOS and Android November 14, 2026, enabling single-prompt song generation across seven musical genres.
- The platform generates complete songs with lyrics, composition, arrangement, and vocals from natural language descriptions, plus instrumental-only mode for content creators.
- Pricing starts at 30 yuan monthly in China (150 songs) and $14.90 internationally, backed by a strategic Taihe Music copyright partnership.


Alibaba officially released HappyShrimp, its end-to-end AI music creation platform, on iOS and Android on November 14, 2026. The mobile launch brings[text-to-song generation](https://emergent.sh/ai-web-app-builder/music-generator) to consumers worldwide after an initial web beta in August 2026, positioning Alibaba's ATH (TokenHub) business group as a direct competitor in the generative music space dominated by platforms like Suno and Udio.


## Complete Song Generation from Single Prompts


HappyShrimp enables users to generate full songs including lyrics, composition, arrangement, and vocals from a single natural language prompt. The platform supports seven musical styles: Chinese pop, R&B, rock, funk, electronic, classical, and jazz. Users can describe mood, narrative, or stylistic preferences in conversational language, or upload their own lyrics for the AI to set to music.


The platform offers two core generation modes. Smart Lyrics mode produces complete songs with vocals, while Instrumental mode generates background music without lyrics, targeting content creators building soundtracks for short videos, podcasts, and documentaries. A Music Recipe feature allows users to save and reuse generation parameters across sessions, streamlining workflow for creators producing multiple tracks with consistent sonic characteristics.


## Style Reference Without Voice Cloning


The Make a Similar Track function lets users upload reference audio to guide instrumentation and arrangement direction. Alibaba explicitly clarified the feature does not replicate original singer timbre, addressing copyright and ethical concerns that have complicated other generative music platforms. This technical limitation distinguishes HappyShrimp from voice-cloning tools while still offering creative flexibility for producers seeking specific sonic templates.


## Pricing and Copyright Strategy


Standard membership in China costs approximately 30 yuan monthly (around $4.20 USD) and includes 150 song generations, translating to roughly 0.2 yuan per song. International pricing starts at $14.90 per month, with credit packs available from $9.90 for users seeking pay-as-you-go flexibility. The pricing undercuts several Western competitors while remaining accessible to independent creators and small production teams.


Alibaba launched HappyShrimp with a strategic copyright partnership with Taihe Music Group, integrating rights holders into the platform ecosystem from day one. This partnership marks a deliberate contrast to Alibaba's previous music venture: Xiami Music, a streaming service that ceased operations in February 2021. The Taihe collaboration signals Alibaba's intent to build a sustainable generative music business anchored in licensed content and industry collaboration rather than pure consumer streaming.


## Release Date and Platform Details


Officially launched on November 14, 2026, HappyShrimp version 0.2.14 is now available on Apple's App Store and major Android app stores globally. The mobile release follows the August 17, 2026 web beta, marking HappyShrimp as the third product in Alibaba's Happy Series of generative AI models. The series began with HappyHorse, a video generation model, and HappyOyster, a 3D interactive video platform, demonstrating Alibaba's multimodal AI strategy across text, audio, and visual content creation.


## What This Means


HappyShrimp's launch expands Alibaba's footprint in consumer-facing generative AI and challenges Western platforms in the rapidly commoditizing text-to-music market. The Taihe Music partnership and explicit anti-cloning stance suggest Alibaba is prioritizing regulatory compliance and industry relationships over feature parity with more permissive competitors. For creators, the platform offers a cost-effective alternative with localized Chinese music style support and flexible instrumental generation for multimedia workflows. The mobile-first rollout positions HappyShrimp for mainstream adoption beyond the early-adopter web beta audience.
